en.headline: Police arrest three in craft beer machine investment scam involving over HK$4 million
en.dek: Commercial Crime Bureau officers detained a director, office manager and recruiter after six mostly elderly victims reported losses from a scheme promising 60 per cent annual returns.
body: Police have arrested three people in connection with an investment scam that used craft beer machines as a lure and resulted in losses of more than HK$4 million for at least six victims, most of them elderly.

Officers from the Commercial Crime Bureau’s Deception Investigation Unit said the syndicate began promoting the scheme in November last year. Investors were told the machines would be leased to outlets on the mainland, guaranteeing annual returns of up to 60 per cent and full repayment of principal after two years.

To build trust, the group organised investment seminars, restaurant gatherings and festival events, and invited prospects to a Jordan office for tours and beer tastings, police said. Initial interest payments were made, but the company later suspended them before announcing a reduction to 6 per cent.

Investigators found the firm had no genuine operations in Hong Kong beyond raising funds and had taken no substantive steps toward any listing. Part of the victims’ money was transferred to personal securities accounts, police said.

On Friday, officers raided the Jordan office and related residences, arresting two men and a woman aged between 46 and 54 on suspicion of conspiracy to defraud. The three were described as a company director, an office manager and a recruiter. Police seized investment contracts, about HK$80,000 in cash, mobile phones and promotional materials. The case remains under investigation, and officers are contacting other potential investors.

zh.headline: 手工啤酒機投資騙案警拘3人 至少6名長者涉款逾400萬
zh.dek: 商罪科昨日行動拘捕公司董事、辦事處負責人及招攬者，初步接觸6名多為長者的受害人，合共投資超過400萬元。
body: 警方商業罪案調查科偵破一宗以手工啤酒機為招徠的投資騙案，拘捕三人，最少六名市民受騙，損失超過400萬港元，受害人大部分為長者。
警方表示，涉案集團自去年11月起以「保本」及高回報作招徠，誘使市民投資手工啤酒機，聲稱機器會出租至內地，保證年利率高達60%，兩年後可全數取回本金。
為建立信任，集團舉辦投資講座、酒樓聚餐及節日聯誼活動，並帶受害人到佐敦辦事處參觀及試飲啤酒。警方指，集團起初有派發利息，其後暫停，再宣布將回報率大幅調低至6%。
調查發現，該集團在香港除收取資金外並無任何實際營運，亦無任何上市實質行動。部分投資款項更被轉至私人證券戶口。
警方昨日突擊搜查佐敦辦事處及相關住所，以涉嫌串謀詐騙拘捕兩男一女，年齡介乎46至54歲，分別報稱公司董事、辦事處負責人及負責招募投資者的上線。行動中檢獲投資合約、約8萬元現金、手機及推廣物資。案件仍在調查，警方正聯絡其他潛在投資者。
更正：中文版本文字已更正編碼錯誤。
